title: Going to the Moon
examples: What did the astronauts wear when they went to the Moon?
How did the rockets get to space?
What is special about the Moon's surface?

explain.say: Today you will learn how people went to the Moon.
Rockets have powerful engines. The engines push the rocket up into space.
Astronauts are people trained to travel in space.
Astronauts walked on the Moon. They left footprints in the dust.
In 1969, Apollo 11 landed the first people on the Moon.
Today, rockets carry satellites and astronauts into space.

faq.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
faq.a: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon. He was part of the Apollo 11 mission.
asks: Who walked on the Moon first?
Which astronaut first stepped on the Moon?
Who was the first Moon walker?

faq.a: A spacesuit gives astronauts air to breathe. It keeps them safe in space.
asks: Why do astronauts wear big suits?
What keeps astronauts safe in space?
What is the purpose of a spacesuit?

faq.a: Rockets work by burning fuel to create hot gas. This gas pushes the rocket out the back very fast.
asks: What makes a rocket go fast?
How does a rocket get off the ground?

faq.q: Do footprints on the Moon last forever?
faq.a: They last a very long time. The Moon has no wind or rain to wipe them away.
asks: Why do Moon footprints stay put?

faq.a: Apollo 11 was the specific mission that successfully landed humans on the Moon in 1969.
asks: When did humans reach the Moon?
What mission landed people on the Moon?

facts: Rockets use powerful engines to travel through space.
Astronauts wear special suits to stay safe in space.
Apollo 11 landed humans on the Moon in 1969.
Footprints left on the Moon can stay visible for a long time.

quiz.say: What pushes a rocket up into space?
quiz.why: The engines burn fuel. The hot gas pushes the rocket up.

wrong.1: Wind can blow a kite, but it is far too weak for a rocket.
wrong.2: The Moon is far away, and it pushes nothing up.

quiz.say: What do astronauts train to do?
quiz.why: Astronauts train so they can live and work safely in space.

wrong.0: Engineers build rockets, and astronauts fly in them.
wrong.2: Some astronauts walked on the Moon, but most work on space stations.

quiz.say: What did astronauts leave on the Moon's dusty ground?
quiz.show: 🌕 What did they leave in the dust?
quiz.why: Astronauts walked in the Moon dust. Their footprints are still there.

wrong.0: The Moon has no rain, so there are no puddles.
wrong.1: Plants need air and water, and the Moon has neither.
